name: Codemonkey
description: A minimalist typing-speed test for developers: like Monkeytype, but you type real code snippets in 10 languages and get WPM, accuracy and consistency. Vanilla JS, no backend. 🍂

paragraphs: Monkeytype, but for code. A minimalist typing‑speed test where you type real code snippets and measure your WPM, accuracy, and consistency — no sign‑up, no backend, no build step.

Codemonkey is a browser typing test for programmers who want to practise typing real code instead of prose. It is a static site in plain HTML, CSS and JavaScript with no build step and no backend, hosted on GitHub Pages. Status: working and live; a small personal project with hand-written snippets in 10 languages.

Typing tests use prose. But the stuff developers actually type all day — brackets, semicolons, camelCase, indentation — never shows up. codemonkey drops real, idiomatic code in front of you and clocks how fast you can type it, the same clean way Monkeytype does for words.
features: A near‑endless pool of correct content — 281 hand‑written code snippets across 10 languages

(JavaScript · Python · TypeScript · Java · C++ · Go · Rust · SQL · Bash · Sprout), the mainstream ones each verified to compile or parse, plus a quotes mode of 70 famous programming & wisdom lines. No immediate repeats,…
Smart auto‑indentation — press Enter and the next line's leading whitespace is
filled in for you, so you only ever type the characters that matter (more below).
time — type as much as you can in 15 / 30 / 60 / 120 seconds.
